description.narrative: The most significant expected project-level impact is the increase of access to finance for micro and small businesses in Guyana, including women, smallholder farmers and those located in the Hinterlands. The project will primarily support the lending to smallholder farmers, thus enabling IPED to extend its tailored financial services and business training to more borrowers in the agricultural sector, which is underserved by commercial banks in the country. At market-level, IFCs investment is expected to contribute to climate resilience in the Caribbean by demonstrating a natural disaster-linked deferral option offered by IPED to its MSME borrowers.

The proposed project consists of a senior loan of up to US$7 million to the Institute of Private Enterprise Development Limited (IPED, or the Institute). The loan proceeds will support the expansion of IPEDs lending operations, targeting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME), with a particular focus on smallholder farmers, women-owned businesses, and potentially refugees and recent migrants in Guyana.
